neighbours.label: A present-tense verb, or 'do', in a generic or habitual statement or question (what happens, I go to, what do you make of); the same sentence in the past tense stays quiet
fire: What do you think of the new coach?
This is what happens when nobody reads the rules.
I go to college near my parents' house.
What Do You Say to a Grieving Friend?
How do you make a good omelette?
Most people here go to work by bus.
Here is what happens if you skip a dose.
We do our shopping at the market on Mondays.
quiet: What did you think of the new coach?
This is what happened when nobody read the rules.
I went to college near my parents' house.
What Did You Say to a Grieving Friend?
How did you make such a good omelette?
Most people here went to work by bus.
Here is what happened after you skipped a dose.
We did our shopping at the market on Monday.

short: verb in the generic present tense
notes: Card: ' make' x4, ' happens' x3, ' do' x2, ' does' x2, ' go', ' only', Arabic present-tense ' ي' x3 (the present prefix). Logit effect of the + pole promotes ' use', ' do', ' regularly'. Probe, each against its past-tense twin: what happens 0.56 vs 0.02, What Do You Do 0.69 vs 0.01, make of it 0.34 vs 0.01, I go 0.29 vs 0.02. ' only' 0.20 in both, so that peak is not about tense.
